intent: Hold the iteration-7 geometry unchanged (five sensors at y = 0.07 m, x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.16 by 0.14 m body, 0.6 kg) so the Integrator's larger-ki controller is the only variable. Expect oval and s-bend to hold at 20 of 20, and the slalom to move only if the integral term corrects the motor-mismatch bias. Next geometry step, planned but not yet committed: test wheel_track of about 0.10 m at y = 0.07 m in the following iteration, to see whether a narrower track speeds the slalom reversal. Revert to y = 0.06 m only if oval or s-bend completion falls below 20 of 20 and 18 of 20. Widen the spread to x = ±0.032 m only if slalom line losses rise above about 2 per run with progress below 0.2.
learning: Iterations 5 to 7 show that y = 0.07 m reduced oval and s-bend max_error and gave no further slalom gain, so look-ahead is saturated. Iteration 7 is the first race where the slalom progress reached about 0.3 with line losses near 1 per run, which makes the reversal-reaction hypothesis the live one. Hypotheses for this race: (1) with geometry held, slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m, which would show the controller change alone does not clear the reversal limit; (2) slalom progress rises above 0.32 if the integral term helps; (3) oval and s-bend completion hold at 20 of 20 and about 18 to 20 of 20. If (2) holds, the controller is the lever and geometry stays put. If the slalom still fails with the same error signature, the next geometry test is wheel_track near 0.10 m.
rationale: Iteration 7 (y = 0.07 m, x = ±0.024 m, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track) scored 673.6, the best so far. Oval and s-bend both complete 20 of 20. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, with progress 0.3185, max_error 0.0632 m and 1.0 line-loss events per run. Those numbers match the Integrator's trigger for a wheel_track test (progress near 0.3, max_error near 0.063 m, line losses near 1 per run), so the trigger condition is met. The Integrator also asked that the controller change be tested with geometry held, and that wheel_track only be tested after that controller race has been separated out. This iteration carries the Integrator's larger-ki controller candidate. Changing wheel_track now would confound that result, so I am taking their sequencing advice and holding the geometry exactly as in iterations 5 to 7. I am deferring the wheel_track test (0.10 m) to the next geometry step, when it can be read against a clean controller baseline. Line losses are far below the 2-per-run widening threshold, and the sensor spread is not the limit. The body and mass are not constraints, and the off-track limit stays at its 0.06 m floor. I expect oval and s-bend to hold at 20 of 20 and the slalom to stay limited by reversal reaction unless the ki change helps it. I am not stating a score outcome for the controller change.
